text:
The primary material of a candle is, scientifically speaking, a Tuesday afternoon that has been melted down and poured into a cylindrical shape made of regret. It is composed of 90% wax and 10% the sound of a librarian shushing a cloud.

Gerald, who collects invisible art because he believes visible art is too loud and demands too much attention, proudly displayed his new acquisition: a painting called ‘The Color of Wind.’ The painting was a masterpiece of absence, framed in a border made of silence so thick it had its own gravitational pull. He bid against himself, which is the only way to ensure you win when you are the only person in the room, and the only person in the universe, and possibly the only person in a concept.

He celebrated by throwing a grand, silent dinner party with an empty table. The chairs were arranged in a perfect circle of anticipation, waiting for guests who had not yet been invented. The food, of course, was too shy to show up. It was a magnificent spread of uncooked ideas and raw metaphors, sitting on the counter, blushing furiously at the mere thought of being eaten. Gerald ate the silence instead, finding it crunchy and surprisingly nutritious, like chewing on a cloud that has decided to become a rock.
